title: MGSER-SAM: Memory-Guided Soft Experience Replay with Sharpness-Aware Optimization for Enhanced Continual Learning
venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
publication_status_observed: arXiv:2405.09492v1 [cs.LG] 15 May 2024; venue listed as IEEE IJCNN in paper header
main_claims: Integrating SAM into experience replay-based continual learning (ER-SAM) improves generalisation by finding flatter minima, and is scalable to other ER-like methods.
MGSER-SAM addresses weight perturbation direction conflicts between current-task gradients and memory buffer gradients using soft logits and gradient direction alignment.
MGSER-SAM outperforms ER and DER++ baselines by 24.4% and 17.6% in test accuracy respectively, while achieving the lowest forgetting across all three CL scenarios.
methodology: The authors first integrate the SAM optimiser into Experience Replay (ER-SAM) as a baseline. They then propose MGSER-SAM, which addresses conflicts between weight perturbation directions for current tasks and memory buffer samples by: (1) using soft logits (soft cross-entropy rather than hard labels for memory samples) to smooth the gradient directions, and (2) aligning memory gradient directions with the current task gradient to reduce conflicts. Experiments are conducted on Split-CIFAR-10, Split-CIFAR-100, Split-TinyImageNet, and Permuted-MNIST across task-IL, domain-IL, and class-IL settings.
key_results: MGSER-SAM improves testing accuracy by 24.4% over ER and 17.6% over DER++ when averaged across benchmarks.
MGSER-SAM achieves the lowest forgetting score on each benchmark compared to ER, DER++, and ER-SAM.
SAM integration alone (ER-SAM) provides meaningful improvement over standard ER, validating that flatness optimisation benefits replay-based CL.
limitations: The method is specific to replay-based continual learning; no analysis of OOD generalisation under distributional shift is provided.
The soft logits approach adds a design choice (temperature) that requires tuning.
Comparison is limited to ER-based methods; other CL categories (regularisation, expansion) are not evaluated.
relevance_to_rq: This paper applies SAM in a continual learning replay setting, not the OOD corruption benchmarks of the RQ. While it demonstrates SAM's utility for generalisation via flatness in a different domain, it does not address the SAM-vs-SWA flatness comparison, CKA representation stability, or CIFAR-C evaluations central to the RQ.
